critic_text:
I need the actual change, not just the narrative of the error — I'll locate the BLOCKED contract, the probe rule, and the sweep before judging whether absence can still be asserted.
The review artifacts and the BLOCKED-correction unit look like the actual subject — I'll read those next rather than judging the narrative alone.
The widened scope moves the rule onto the BLOCKED write-path, requires probe evidence to unblock, extends coverage to every precondition-evaluating agent, and adds a report-only sweep. That is the right shape. It does not close the method error.

Previous blockers, one by one:

1. Canonical probe / “cannot probe” terminal — **not closed.** Model-family reachability still has no named listing command. The predicate says the contract must say what happens when no probe is known, then does not say it. There is still no terminal distinct from BLOCKED.
2. Sibling agents — **not closed.** Item 3 is a coverage sentence. The only mechanism in item 1 is a BLOCKED transition. Paths that assert the same precondition without writing BLOCKED are untouched.
3. Detection signal — **partially closed.** A report-only sweep will see records with a missing probe field. It will not see a record whose attached “probe” is the original absence check. That is the incident class.

What remains is the original substitution: a local-marker observation offered as measurement of live capability.

Severity: high
Mechanism: Item 1 requires a BLOCKED transition to carry “the probe,” and the rule denylists two evidence shapes (absent config file, env-var proxy). It never defines a valid capability probe, never names the listing command that would have shown seven reachable models, and never gives a legal move when no probe is known. The original env/file checks *are* probes — of marker absence. An agent that does not know the listing command will attach a marker command (`test -f …`, `printenv …`, or a third shape: missing directory, empty `which`, denied-tool exit). The write-path is satisfied. BLOCKED is written. The predicate that “the contract has to say what happens when no probe is known” is an admission, not a terminal.
Failure mode: Same false BLOCKED as the incident, now with a probe field filled by an absence observation. Work stops while models are reachable. Alternatively the agent invents a third marker shape the denylist does not name and the transition accepts it.
Detection signal: A BLOCKED record whose attached command/output is a file-existence, env-unset, PATH-miss, or empty-listing observation, while the models-list command still returns multiple families. The specified sweep, looking for “asserted without probing,” will not flag it.
Falsifier: The transition contract (a) names a CANNOT_PROBE / UNPROBED terminal distinct from BLOCKED, (b) makes absence-of-local-marker ineligible as evidence for a capability precondition — not a two-shape denylist, (c) names the listing command as the probe for model-family reachability, and (d) refuses BLOCKED when no probe is known rather than accepting a substitute. Evidence of that text in the contract would change this.
Recommendation: Add that terminal. Forbid absence-only observations as capability evidence. Name the listing command for this precondition. When no probe is known, the legal write is CANNOT_PROBE (prior state preserved, operator-visible), never BLOCKED.

Severity: high
Mechanism: Item 3 says the rule reaches every agent that evaluates a precondition. The only specified mechanism is the BLOCKED write-path in item 1. CPD dispatch, critic_panel assembly, review, and resume can still infer “no second family” from the same absent env/config and silently drop to one family or skip the debate without ever writing BLOCKED. The sweep only inspects records, so those assertions never become a detection signal.
Failure mode: The unit is unblocked with a real listing attached; the next gate re-asserts unreachability from the same markers and under-invokes the panel. The false BLOCKED becomes a false single-family run.
Detection signal: After this scope, unset provider keys, omit the harness file, run the listing command (it still returns seven models), then exercise dispatch/review/panel construction. If any path omits a family or skips CPD without attaching that listing, the class is still open.
Falsifier: A single write-path invariant that every capability-negative decision — BLOCKED *and* panel construction / dispatch / review — must attach a capability-probe transcript, plus a test that missing env+config alone cannot BLOCK or shrink the panel when the listing returns models.
Recommendation: Lift the probe-evidence invariant off the BLOCKED verb onto every capability-negative write. Keep the sweep report-only, but score absence-shaped evidence as a hit, not only a missing probe field.

The unblock-with-transcript rule (item 2) and append-only answer of the original entry are sound. They do not close the assertion-from-absence path.

- severity: blocker — No cannot-probe terminal; absence still qualifies as the attached “probe,” so BLOCKED can be asserted without a capability measurement.
- severity: major — Probe invariant is specified only on BLOCKED writes; sibling gates can re-assert the same precondition from absence and skip the panel.
verdict: concerns

Severity: high  
Mechanism: The scope says the contract must address unknown probes but does not define a terminal “cannot probe” state or forbid asserting BLOCKED from absence when no probe exists.  
Failure mode: An agent can still treat a missing config file or credential environment variable as proof of unreachability without running a valid probe.  
Detection signal: A sweep finds BLOCKED records whose evidence is only absent-file or absent-environment observations; tests can exercise an arbitrary precondition with no canonical probe.  
Falsifier: The actual transition contract explicitly rejects absence-only evidence and records an auditable “cannot probe” terminal outcome.  
Recommendation: Add that terminal outcome and make absence-only observations ineligible to assert the precondition. The mechanism-carried probe, evidence-backed unblocking, global agent scope, and reporting sweep otherwise close the other stated blockers.

- severity: blocker — No explicit cannot-probe terminal leaves absence-based BLOCKED assertions possible.
verdict: concerns

## Direct answer

The widened scope closes the *observed instance* of the method error at the *named* transition, but it does not close the method error. It converts "assert from absence" from default behavior into a rule violation, while leaving three concrete paths open: a proxy probe attached as evidence passes a presence-only gate; the undefined "cannot probe" case can become an escape hatch; and precondition assertions in records other than BLOCKED/unblock are governed by rule text plus an after-the-fact sweep, not by mechanism.

## The three previous blockers, one by one

**1. "No canonical probe and no cannot-probe terminal" — addressed in intent, not closed as specified.** The scope states the contract "has to say what happens when no probe is known," but what it says is not in front of me, and that paragraph is the load-bearing part of this amendment. Closure requires the terminal to be non-asserting, evidenced, and unavailable to unblocking — see Finding B.

**2. "Sibling agents unamended" — closed as text, open as mechanism.** "The rule reaches every agent that evaluates a precondition" is an instruction. The only mechanism named is that "a transition to BLOCKED carries the probe," plus its answering entry. The scope's own sweep item ("records that asserted one without probing") concedes that other record types assert preconditions; those carry no described gate. See Finding C.

**3. "No detection signal" — partially closed.** A sweep now exists where none did. But it is unspecified in the three ways that decide whether it is a signal or a log: how it mechanically identifies an unprobed assertion, how often it runs, and who must answer its reports. "Reports and never corrects" plus append-only history means a report without a mandatory answering entry terminates in a file. See Findings A (adequacy-blindness) and D (operations).

## Findings

**Finding A — the gate checks presence of a probe, not adequacy of a probe.**
Severity: high
Mechanism: The mechanism gates on a probe being *attached*, and the rule denylists exactly two proxy shapes (absent config file, env-var proxy). Nothing defines adequacy positively — that the probe's output must decide the precondition itself rather than a correlate of it. The phrase "the probe that established the precondition" does not close this: the env-var check was, in the original author's mind, exactly that. Any third correlate — a lockfile, a PID, `which binary` while the daemon is down, a stale registry, credentials checked against the wrong endpoint — attaches cleanly and satisfies the gate.
Failure mode: The original incident replays in costume. The record carries a populated "probe" field containing a proxy check, the schema validates, the BLOCKED stands, and the false precondition now looks evidenced.
Detection signal: A sweep or validator that replays attached commands and flags outputs that do not decide the stated precondition. No such adequacy check is described; the described sweep looks for records "without probing," i.e., absence, not wrongness.
Falsifier: Show the contract's positive definition of an adequate probe (output directly decides the precondition's truth condition) and a gate or sweep that validates probe type, not just presence. I would withdraw this finding.
Recommendation: Replace the two-shape denylist with a positive adequacy criterion — "a probe of P is an operation whose output directly decides P; correlates (credential presence, config existence, cached state) are not probes of P" — keep the two shapes as named examples, and have the sweep flag correlate-patterned probe commands.

**Finding B — the "cannot probe" terminal is obligated but unspecified, and the obvious version recreates the error.**
Severity: high
Mechanism: The fifth predicate requires the contract to define the no-probe case, but the terminal's content is not in the scope under review. If it permits recording BLOCKED-on-P (or "unreachable") from "no probe known," the method error recurs one level up: absence of a probe asserted from absence of discovery. The original failure was precisely an undiscovered enumeration command — seven models, one command, never run.
Failure mode: An agent records "no probe known → BLOCKED," reaching the incident's conclusion by a shorter route; or records "no probe known → proceed," asserting the precondition's satisfiability from the same absence. Both pass any presence-only gate.
Detection signal: Cannot-probe records with empty or boilerplate discovery-effort fields; cannot-probe records naming no introspection surface (list / doctor / --help) of the target system. None specified.
Falsifier: Produce the terminal's definition showing it (i) records neither P nor ¬P — the unit is held on *verification*, not on the precondition; (ii) requires attached discovery-effort evidence (commands run, outputs); (iii) is unavailable to unblocking entries. Absent that text, this stands.
Recommendation: Define the terminal as INDETERMINATE(P): it blocks the unit on verification, must carry the discovery commands and their outputs, and can never unblock; an unblock requires a positive probe, full stop.

**Finding C — universal reach is asserted as rule, but only two transitions are mechanized.**
Severity: medium
Mechanism: The named mechanism is the BLOCKED transition and its answer. Everything else that asserts a precondition — readiness claims, "dependency confirmed" notes, proceed records — is covered by "the rule reaches every agent," which is policy text. The incident originated in an agent's method failure; rule text is precisely what that population does not reliably execute.
Failure mode: A sibling agent writes "dependency reachable, proceeding" with no probe; nothing rejects the write; dependent work consumes the false assertion before any sweep runs.
Detection signal: Sweep hits on non-BLOCKED records — but the sweep is the only backstop and is itself unspecified (Finding D). A write-time rejection does not exist outside block/unblock.
Falsifier: Show that all precondition-asserting transition types share the probe-carrying schema, or an explicit, reasoned acceptance that rule-plus-sweep is sufficient for named lower-stakes record types.
Recommendation: Extend the probe-attachment requirement to every transition whose record asserts or denies a precondition; where that is genuinely infeasible, enumerate the exempt record types and the reason, so the sweep's target set is exact rather than open-ended.

**Finding D — the sweep's method, cadence, and consumer are unspecified.**
Severity: low
Mechanism: "The sweep looks for existing records that asserted one without probing." Identifying a precondition assertion in an arbitrary record is a classification problem; no method, cadence, or mandated consumer is stated, and "reports and never corrects" makes the report the end of the line unless an answering entry is required elsewhere.
Failure mode: The sweep emits a report nobody must answer; append-only history means flagged false assertions stand uncontradicted in the record consumers actually read.
Detection signal: Sweep-report count versus answering-entry count; a growing gap is the tell.
Falsifier: Produce the classification method (trivial for structured records — absent probe field; named patterns for free text) and a rule that every hit gets an answering entry.
Recommendation: Specify method, cadence, and a mandatory answering-entry rule per sweep hit.

**Finding E — attached output is not replayable and carries no recency semantics.**
Severity: low
Mechanism: "Attaches the probe command and its output" — output is self-reported text. Without exact invocation, exit code, timestamp, and host context, the attachment is an assertion about an assertion. Reachability is also time-varying; an undated probe decays silently.
Failure mode: A truncated, mis-pasted, or fabricated output passes review because it cannot be re-run; or a stale-but-genuine probe is consumed weeks later as current truth.
Detection signal: Replay attempts on attached probes; missing exit codes/timestamps; probe age versus consumption date.
Falsifier: Show the schema requires command, args, exit code, timestamp, host context, and that consumers re-probe or enforce recency for time-varying preconditions.
Recommendation: Require replayable probe records and a consume-time recency rule for time-varying preconditions.

## What remains

A positive adequacy definition for probes (A); a specified, non-asserting, evidence-carrying INDETERMINATE terminal that cannot unblock (B); mechanical gating — or an explicit, reasoned exemption list — for precondition assertions outside the block/unblock pair (C); an operational sweep with mandated answering entries (D); replayable, timestamped probe records (E). None of these requires new machinery beyond what the scope already builds; all are amendments to the same contract.

- severity: major — Probe gate checks presence, not adequacy; an unnamed third proxy shape attached as evidence passes, replaying the incident in costume.
- severity: major — "Cannot probe" terminal is obligated but unspecified; if it asserts or blocks on the precondition it recreates the error one level up.
- severity: major — Universal reach is rule text; only BLOCKED/unblock transitions are mechanically gated, other asserting records rely on post-hoc sweep.
- severity: minor — Sweep's classification method, cadence, and mandatory answering entry are unspecified; reports can terminate unread.
- severity: minor — Attached probe output is not replayable (no invocation/exit code/timestamp) and no recency rule exists for time-varying reachability.
verdict: concerns
